solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sea-sport star wearing red emerged from water again

indicators.note: the sport and the star are worn inside the colour, as if dressed in it

parts.note: taken as the letters as written
surfing is a sport played on the sea, giving surf
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A champion surfer in a red wetsuit comes up out of the waves once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back up to the surface of water after diving is exactly that verb's meaning.

clue.text: Choose dark rice for cooking — do this with fine lady in prospect!

definitions.text: do this with fine lady in prospect!

indicators.note: food being cooked is transformed, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to pick dark rice, then a strange aside about a fine lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the nursery rhyme 'Ride a cock horse to Banbury Cross, to see a fine lady upon a white horse'; Banbury is an English market town.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's rider sets out on a hobby-horse precisely to go and see the fine lady.

clue.text: That is little fellow, betrayed earlier, to keep going

indicators.note: tells us the word for betrayed goes in front of the other pieces

parts.note: to sell someone out is to betray them, so sold
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
Ron is a short form of the man's name Ronald

explanation.surface: Someone describes a little man who was let down in the past yet still carries on.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist doggedly through difficulty is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Perform again and swing back the other way

definitions.meaning: to act a part once more
to respond by moving in the opposite direction, as a pendulum or market does

explanation.surface: An actor repeats a show and a pendulum swings back.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-act it means perform again; as a whole word it means respond in the opposite direction.

clue.text: A string's holding together soft plants

indicators.note: the string is holding the soft letter within it

parts.note: a string is a line; line's gives the letters with its S
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Something about a string binding together delicate plants in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpines are small mountain plants grown in rockeries, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Most weird estate flooded by lake

indicators.note: the lake pours into the estate, filling its middle

parts.note: Est. is the abbreviation for estate
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A strange housing estate that has been swamped by a nearby lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means uncanny or weird, so its superlative is the weirdest.

clue.text: Centre of operations devoid of morality

definitions.meaning: a headquarters from which activities are run

explanation.surface: A headquarters run by people with no morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning headquarters and an adjective meaning ignoble share one spelling.

clue.text: Stop a large vessel crossing sea initially

indicators.note: the vessel lies across the sea's letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a vat is a large tank or tub

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word sea

explanation.surface: A command to halt a big ship that is making its way over the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the nautical command to stop or cease.

clue.text: Heroic men at sea netting 500 starfish maybe

indicators.note: the anagram catches the number inside it as a net would
confused, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Brave sailors on the ocean catching a large haul of starfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns HEROICMEN into ECHINOERM, and 'netting' puts D inside it after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Starfish belong to the echinoderm phylum, so a starfish is an example.

clue.text: Woman was poorly on return journey

indicators.note: coming back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to be poorly is to be ill, so ailed

explanation.surface: A woman fell ill while travelling home.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Block of words soldier attached to chart

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Some writing pinned by a soldier to a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a distinct section of text, a block of words.

clue.text: Approach snooker table and fall apart

definitions.meaning: to go to the pot, as a player does to pot a ball

explanation.surface: A snooker player walks up to the table and goes to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue sport like pool; to pot is to knock a ball into a pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase is read literally as walking to the pot and idiomatically as falling into ruin.

clue.text: How we count with energy concentrated

parts.note: we count in tens with a decimal system
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A description of counting done with great vigour and focus.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means highly concentrated, as in a strong flavour or focus.

clue.text: Bird appearing before a new moon

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird shows up just before the new moon rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new moon' reads as one phrase, but 'new' is wordplay and 'moon' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn.

clue.text: See 1
Goods vehicle makes journey

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
goes means travels, makes a journey

explanation.surface: A goods vehicle sets off on its trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargoes are loads of goods carried by ship or plane, so the plural noun matches goods.

clue.text: Descending mountain when there are fewer fellow-travellers

parts.note: coming down off something
a peak is a mountain top

explanation.surface: Coming down a mountain at a quiet time with few other walkers about.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak travel is at quieter times, when fewer passengers share the trains.

clue.text: Record Socialist dwindling to nothing?

parts.note: to tape something is to record it
a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A recording of a left-wing politician whose support is fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually to a point, almost nothing.

clue.text: First principles allowing inferior little types to pocket money

indicators.note: the small types take the coin into their pocket, so it sits inside

parts.note: runts are undersized, weak creatures
a dime is a ten-cent US coin

explanation.surface: Basic rules that let small inferior people pocket some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudiments are the basic principles of a subject, its first elements.

clue.text: Talk together having hugged one sort of tree

indicators.note: the talking word wraps round the single letter as an embrace

parts.note: to confer is to consult together
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: People chat after embracing a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as a pine or fir.

clue.text: Artist getting about nibbled a toastie

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
re means about or concerning
bit is the past tense of bite, close to nibbled

explanation.surface: A painter going around nibbling on a toasted sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a kind of toasted snack.

clue.text: Fighter in army surrounded by loony men

indicators.note: the army letters sit inside the crazy word

parts.note: loony means crazy, mad
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A soldier caught among a crowd of crazy men.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull.

clue.text: Odd dream is interpreted incorrectly

indicators.note: strange, so the letters of the next two words are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange dream has been wrongly explained.
explanation.definitionFit: To misread is to understand or interpret something wrongly.

clue.text: Author publishes sermons, but only five of them

indicators.note: just five letters are taken from within the two words

explanation.surface: A writer brings out sermons, but just five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five of them' seems to count sermons; it counts letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was a German-born novelist, author of Siddhartha.

clue.text: Separate prophet, very confined

indicators.note: the very letter is shut up inside the prophet

parts.note: a seer is someone who foresees, a prophet

explanation.surface: Keep apart a prophet who is closely shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut apart, to separate.

clue.text: Platform nonsense about end of NHS — bizarre!

indicators.note: the nonsense goes round the final letter

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense

indicators.note: takes only the closing letter of NHS

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd, bizarre

explanation.surface: A speaker on a platform raves about the National Health Service ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: See old lover thwarted

parts.note: the Holy See is based in Rome

explanation.surface: Look at an old flame who was frustrated in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is the bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo is the archetypal lover whose love is thwarted by feuding families.

clue.text: Company man coming out as 'not the proper article'?

indicators.note: the letters of man leave the word company

explanation.surface: An employee comes out, asking if he is the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is a reproduction rather than the genuine original.

clue.text: Cleric, all right and competent, that can be countermanded

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
OK means all right
able means competent

explanation.surface: A capable clergyman describing an order that can be cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Revokable means able to be revoked, cancelled or countermanded.

clue.text: Fruit to disappear — taken by staff

indicators.note: the disappearing word is taken up by the staffing word, which comes before it

parts.note: to man something is to staff it
to go is to vanish, disappear

explanation.surface: Fruit vanishes after the workers take it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Modern money a setback for old French street

indicators.note: a setback turns things backwards, so the street is read in reverse

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Modern currency is a setback for an old street in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency adopted by many EU countries since 1999.

clue.text: Boss I love leads university, crafty in a bookish way

indicators.note: the first pieces go in front of the university letter

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob
O is love, zero in tennis
sly means crafty

explanation.surface: A boss saying I love leading a university, cunning and scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: Studiously means with dedication to study, in a scholarly manner.
